title: Long COVID
summary: What is long COVID?COVID-19 (coronavirus disease 2019) is an illness caused by a virus. Many people get better within a few days or weeks after being infected with the virus. But if you have symptoms that last for at least three months or more, you may have long COVID. Long COVID is a chronic (long-lasting) condition. It includes a wide range of symptoms or conditions that can range from mild to severe. You may:Have symptoms that linger for weeks, months, or even yearsSeem to recover from COVID-19 but then see your symptoms returnDevelop new symptoms or new health conditions within a few months of having COVID-19There are several other names for long COVID. It can also be called post-COVID conditions, long-haul COVID, and post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 (PASC).Who is more likely to develop long COVID?Anyone who had COVID-19, whether it was severe or mild, can have long-lasting symptoms. But you are at higher risk of long COVID if you:Are female.Are Hispanic or Latino.Had severe COVID-19 illness, especially if you were hospitalized or needed intensive care.Had other health conditions before you got COVID-19.Did not get a COVID-19 vaccine.Had multisystem inflammatory syndrome (MIS)
